chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“Whoever says, in the last sajdah of the nāfilah after al-Maghrib on the night of al-Jumuʿah—and if he says it every night, then that is better—: ‘O Allah, I ask You by Your Noble Face and Your Great Name to send blessings upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and to forgive me my great sin,’ seven times, he departs while he has been forgiven.”

He said, and he عليه السلام said: “When Thursday evening and the night of al-Jumuʿah come, angels descend from the heaven with pens of gold and sheets of silver. They do not write on Thursday evening, the night of al-Jumuʿah, and the day of al-Jumuʿah until the sun sets anything except blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.”

key_terms.اسْمِكَ الْعَظِيمِ: Your Great Name, invoking Allah through His exalted name
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ: sending blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: the recommended prayer in which this supplication is recited
key_terms.بِوَجْهِكَ الْكَرِيمِ: by Your Noble Face, an expression of invoking Allah through His majesty and honor
key_terms.ذَنْبِيَ الْعَظِيمَ: my great sin, referring to the supplicant’s plea for forgiveness
key_terms.سَجْدَةٍ: a prostration within prayer, specifically the final sajdah mentioned here
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْجُمُعَةِ: the night preceding Friday, identified as a specially virtuous time
key_terms.مَلَائِكَةٌ: angels who descend at the specified blessed time

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited after Maghrib on the night of Jumuʿah for forgiveness?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a specific du'a to be recited in the final sajdah of the nāfilah after Maghrib on the night of Jumuʿah, promising forgiveness for the one who recites it seven times. It also highlights the special virtue of sending salawat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم during Thursday evening, the night of Jumuʿah, and Friday.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1251 - Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

"Whoever, in the last prostration of a recommended prayer (nafilah) after Maghrib on the night of Jumu’ah—and even better if said every night—recites,
'O’ Allah (swt), I ask You by Your Noble Face and Your Great Name to bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and to forgive me my great sin,' seven times, will rise having been forgiven."

He also said (as): "When Thursday evening and the night of Jumu’ah arrive, angels descend from the heavens carrying golden pens and silver tablets. They write down nothing from Thursday evening, the night of Jumu’ah, and the day of Jumu’ah until sunset except blessings upon The Prophet (sw)”.
